title: Trace-binding guard for invoke endpoints lives in handlers, not auth validators
answers: where to add authorization for trace ids in the invoke routes
why the scorer trace check is not in the auth validator
deployment without basic-auth app still checks trace ownership
body:
Invariant: The trace-to-experiment ownership check for /invoke routes is implemented inside the handler functions in mlflow/server/handlers.py (via _validate_trace_ids_in_experiment), not in the auth validators in mlflow/server/auth.
Enforced by: mlflow/server/handlers.py:_invoke_scorer_handler, _invoke_issue_detection_handler, _invoke_genai_evaluate_handler, all calling the same helper.
What breaks if skipped: Deployments that mount the handlers without the basic-auth app lose the check entirely, and the three invoke endpoints drift apart.
Constraints: The auth validator still gates on experiment UPDATE permission; the handler check is an additional binding, not a replacement. Reviewer note: on plain OSS basic-auth, worker callbacks are rejected by the auth layer, so full content disclosure needs workers with a service identity.
applies: Authorization changes for trace_ids or other object ids referenced by background-job endpoints.
says: Ensure background evaluation jobs verify trace ownership across experiments even without basic authentication.
Prevent users from running scorer or issue detection jobs on unauthorized experiment traces.
Trace authorization checks fail to block access when basic authentication is not enabled.
Evaluation and issue detection endpoints should enforce experiment permissions for all submitted traces.
Running background evaluation on traces from another experiment should be rejected.

In mlflow/server/handlers.py, _validate_trace_ids_in_experiment is called by _invoke_scorer_handler, _invoke_issue_detection_handler, and _invoke_genai_evaluate_handler. This handler-level check ensures deployments mounted without the basic-auth app still verify trace ownership, while auth validators still check experiment UPDATE permission. Guidance applies to background-job authorization changes, noting worker callbacks on plain basic-auth get rejected unless workers use a service identity.
